lessons.topic: Verbs with dative and accusative object (Verben mit Dativ- und Akkusativobjekt)
lessons.title: Giving something to someone
lessons.summary: With geben, schenken, zeigen the person gets the dative and the thing the accusative: Ich schenke meiner Mutter einen Schal.

cards.title: When do you need it?
cards.body: Presents and celebrations: **Was schenkst du deinem Vater?** **Ich gebe dem Kind ein Eis.** **Kannst du mir das Foto zeigen?** Two objects: a **person** (who gets it) and a **thing** (what).

examples.english: I'm giving my girlfriend a book.

cards.title: Person = dative, thing = accusative
cards.body: Ask **Wem?** (to whom) → dative. Ask **Was?** → accusative. Verbs: **geben, schenken, zeigen, bringen, kaufen, schicken, erklären, empfehlen**.
cards.tip: Dative endings: -m, -r, -m, -n. 'm r m n' — say it like a little song.

cards.title: Pronouns in the dative
cards.body: The people often appear as pronouns: **mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen**.

examples.english: Can you give me the salt?

cards.title: Order: person before thing
cards.body: With two **nouns**, the dative (person) comes **before** the accusative (thing).

examples.english: He shows the guest the room.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Ich gebe den Mann das Buch': the person is dative — **dem** Mann. And the dative plural needs an extra **-n**: den Kinder**n**, den Freunde**n**.

examples.english: She's giving her parents a trip.

games.explanation: der/das → dem, die → der, plural → den + n.
The person who gets something is dative; the thing is accusative.

games.english: I'm giving my brother a bike.

lessons.topic: Verbs with a dative object (Verben mit Dativobjekt)
lessons.title: Verbs with the dative
lessons.summary: Some verbs take only a dative: helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören, schmecken, passen, gratulieren.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Celebrations and presents are full of them: **Das Geschenk gefällt mir!** **Ich gratuliere dir!** **Danke, das passt mir gut.** **Kann ich Ihnen helfen?**

examples.english: I'll help you with the cooking.

cards.title: gefallen: back to front
cards.body: With **gefallen, schmecken, passen, stehen** the **thing** is the subject and the **person** is dative. English 'I like the dress' becomes 'The dress pleases me'.
cards.tip: Plural thing → plural verb: Die Blumen gefallen mir.

cards.title: Dative pronouns
cards.body: ich → **mir**, du → **dir**, er/es → **ihm**, sie → **ihr**, wir → **uns**, ihr → **euch**, sie → **ihnen**, Sie → **Ihnen**.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Ich helfe dich': **Ich helfe dir**. Not 'Ich gefalle das Kleid': **Das Kleid gefällt mir**. And **danken** takes the dative: **Ich danke dir**.

games.explanation: Dative pronouns for helfen, danken, gefallen…
The verb agrees with the thing: singular gefällt, plural gefallen.

lessons.topic: Order of dative and accusative pronouns (Stellung von Personalpronomen)
lessons.title: Ich gebe es dir
lessons.summary: When objects become pronouns the order changes: a pronoun comes before a noun, and the accusative pronoun comes first.

cards.title: When do you need it?
cards.body: In real conversations you don't repeat nouns: **Wann gibst du ihm das Geschenk? – Ich gebe es ihm morgen.** Getting the order right makes you sound natural.

examples.german: Gefällt dir der Schal? Ich schenke **ihn dir**!
examples.english: Do you like the scarf? I'm giving it to you!

cards.title: Rule 1: two nouns
cards.body: Two nouns: **dative before accusative** (person before thing).

examples.english: I give the child the ball.

cards.title: Rule 2: pronoun before noun
cards.body: If one object is a pronoun, the **pronoun comes first**, whatever its case.
cards.tip: Short before long: pronouns are short, so they go first.

cards.title: Rule 3: two pronouns
cards.body: Two pronouns: **accusative before dative**. The 'thing' pronoun (es, ihn, sie) comes first.

examples.english: Can you show it to me?

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Ich gebe dem Kind ihn': the pronoun comes first — **Ich gebe ihn dem Kind**. Not 'Ich gebe dir es': with two pronouns, accusative first — **Ich gebe es dir**.

examples.german: Die Karte? Ich schicke **sie euch** morgen.
examples.english: The card? I'll send it to you tomorrow.

games.english: The book? I'll give it to you tomorrow.

games.explanation: Pronoun before noun; two pronouns: accusative first.

games.prompt: Replace the thing with a pronoun
games.explanation: der → ihn (accusative), die → sie, das → es.
